newsitem.title: INDIA: India sees fiscal deficit at 3 pct of GDP by 2000.
newsitem.headline: India sees fiscal deficit at 3 pct of GDP by 2000.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram was quoted on Wednesday as saying the government was committed to narrowing the fiscal deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by the turn of the century.

United News of India (UNI) quoted Chidambaram as telling parliament that one of the major achievements of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government, which assumed power last June, was to bring down the fiscal deficit.
The government estimates that the fiscal deficit will fall to 5.0 percent of GDP in the 1996/97 financial year ending on March 31, down from 5.8 percent in 1995/96.
It has set a fiscal deficit target of 4.5 percent for 1997/98, and aims to cut the fiscal deficit to below 4.0 percent of GDP in 1998/99, Chidambaram said last month.
UNI said Chidambaram compared reducing the deficit to climbing Mount Everest, where scaling the first 20,000 feet (6,100 metres) was the easiest part of the climb.
